crop.notes: Whole Allen item with headline and decks. The decks also list 'A St. Louisian the First to Give Horses Injections' and general sporting news, which follow below and are rightly left out. The last line is slightly damaged.

ocr.notes: Mostly right, but one meaningful error: the image reads 'Allen states that Corbett offered Paddy Smith... $100 for the receipt', while the transcript says 'he offered'. Also 'regard very highly', not 'revere highly'. Last line partly torn ('...ery highly. Very few know how to [make i]t, however'). Decks not transcribed.

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch reported that Tom Allen would quietly go to Jacksonville for the Corbett-Mitchell fight, avoiding Kentucky, where he was indicted after the Goss fight. He predicted Mitchell would beat Corbett with body blows.

metadata.notes: Masthead: Friday, St. Louis Post-Dispatch, December 29, 1893, page 5, first column.

facts.fact: Allen planned to travel from St. Louis to Jacksonville, Florida, for the Corbett-Mitchell fight, keeping his departure date secret
Allen was indicted in Kentucky for his fight with Joe Goss and had not set foot in Kentucky since; he feared trouble passing through the state, though Kentucky never sought his extradition
Allen predicted Mitchell would beat Corbett by infighting and body blows
facts.quote: Mitchell's forte will be at infighting, and when they come to close quarters the Californian's stomach will suffer.

facts.fact: Allen secured twelve ox tails to make a stomach-hardening jelly to send to Mitchell's training quarters

notes: The current summary says Allen 'recommended' the jelly; he was making it to send to Mitchell. The Kentucky indictment fact relates to the unnumbered facts-index entry about waiting out the statute of limitations in Kentucky. The article says the indictment was 'over a decade ago'; 1876 is the Goss fight year.
